Applies to HTTPS and TLS connections the app originates itself, including provisioning, catalog refresh, onboarding checks, diagnostics metadata lookups, and the built-in RIPDPI browser. Android 17 or newer is required for platform ECH in that owned-stack browser path.
Proxy mode limits browser-native TLS shaping

TLS fingerprint profiles and ECH-aware shaping still apply to traffic the app originates itself, but browser-native TLS, ECH, and UDP ownership stay under the browser and OS in proxy mode. Use VPN mode when you need RIPDPI to control the full transport path.
Choose which payload-statistics model the fake-packet path should counter.
Lower targets produce more ASCII-like padding and are mainly useful against bit-count classifiers.
Maximum extra bytes the runtime may add while shaping fake packets.
Use values near 7920 to approximate encrypted traffic without peaking at maximum entropy.
Allow the native runtime to explore alternate entropy combinations and retain better-performing hints on this network.
Chance from 0.0 to 1.0 that the runtime explores instead of reusing the current best hint.
How long (milliseconds) a single strategy experiment lives before being evaluated. Default: 30 000.
Half-life for exponential decay of per-combo statistics. Longer values make the evolver forget slower. Default: 3 600 000.
Number of consecutive failures before a combo is put in cooldown. Default: 3.
How long (milliseconds) a failing combo is skipped while in cooldown. Default: 300 000.

VPN-only. Today this uses the existing post-handshake UDP rebind path for generic QUIC flows; validated RFC 9000 migration is only available in owned QUIC transports.
Available only in VPN mode because the post-handshake UDP rebind path depends on controlled transport ownership.

A QUIC Initial or handshake alone does not confirm HTTP/3. Response headers confirm HTTP/3 even with an HTTP error. An incomplete body remains incomplete. This control result does not prove provider interference.

p50/p95 are the times at or below which 50/95% of measured round trips fall.
RTT is round-trip time; jitter is its variation. Loss is an estimate from connection failures and retransmissions, not a per-site failure rate.
Destination events: %1$d min window ending %3$s, at most %2$d events. Only observed direct-path signals are counted.
Cumulative for this native runtime; the first sample time is unavailable.
p50/p95/p99: 50/95/99% of sampled latencies fall at or below these approximate values in milliseconds.

QUIC DPLPMTUD measures outbound UDP payload bytes from this device to the selected server on this path. The ACK-confirmed value is a lower bound, not the exact path MTU. An ACK on the return path does not measure its PMTU. The configured ceiling and the interface MTU are separate values. A partial observation does not confirm a completed measurement.
Probe loss can occur during size search. It does not establish a path black hole or a provider restriction. The peer can also limit packet size.
